structured_output.summary: Ellipsoidal 163 ± 45 ppm (S32 only) implies 0.105 Msun; Sector 110 can test it.
reasons: The signal is new: `exofop_tois`, `exofop_ctois` and `published_signal` are empty, `ephemeris_match_likely_sources` and `ephemeris_match_contaminated_stars` are empty, and the verification record shows no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-15. Nothing argues for a drop on grounds of prior knowledge.

The transit is real and repeatable: `MES` 38.93774 in S98, `other_sector_results` S32 TESS-SPOC SNR 45.9 against expected 35.9, `joint_search_snr` 62.5 against `joint_search_highest_null_snr` 16.7, `joint_search_detected` True, `period_pile_up_ratio` 0.2. The all-sector figure shows a flat-bottomed transit with sharp ingress and egress in both the S98 QLP and S32 TESS-SPOC panels.

The dip is on the target: `pixel_verdict` on target with `pixel_verdicts_by_sector` S32 SNR 10.9 and S98 SNR 7.7, best star TIC 264626874 in both. In both difference images the out-of-transit-minus-in-transit peak sits on the target pixel with the free-fit cross on the target. With `nfpp_mean` 0 and `nearby_scenarios_excluded` True, this answers the 'neighbour able to cause dip' caution (`gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip`: G 15.5 at 27" needing 24%, G 15.6 at 57" needing 27%).

The transit shape fits a companion of the target star: `stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio` 0.966, `fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis` 1.11, `odd_even_difference_sigma` 1.30, `secondary_depth_ppm` -18 +/- 34 against `secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm` 157 (the phase-0.5 panel is flat). `transit_grazing` False with `fit_impact_parameter` 0.745 +/- 0.0326, so `planet_radius_earth_radii` 17.68 +/- 0.88 is well constrained and below the 22.4 stellar threshold, though at about 1.6 Jupiter radii it is equally consistent with an inflated giant planet or a brown dwarf / late-M dwarf around this `stellar_radius_solar_radii` 2.89514, LAMOST A1V host (`lamost_spectra`).

The deciding issue is the ellipsoidal caution and the present data cannot settle it. `ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm_by_sector` is S32 163 +/- 45 (3.6 sigma, 600 s TESS-SPOC) and S98 155 +/- 348 (uninformative), so the detection rests on a single sector. If real, `ellipsoidal_companion_mass_solar_masses` 0.105 means the companion is not a planet; a Jupiter-mass companion would produce an amplitude far below 45 ppm at `fit_scaled_semi_major_axis` 6.58. Gaia RV does not decide it: `gaia_rv_variable` False, but `gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses` 0.264 does not exclude 0.105, and with `gaia_vbroad_km_s` 185.1972 the RV precision is poor (`gaia_rv_epoch_scatter_km_s` 11.1). A 3.6 sigma single-sector phase-locked signal on a rapidly rotating A star is suggestive but not strong enough to say the companion is most likely stellar, so I do not propose a drop.

What would decide it: `unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star` is 110. A TESS-SPOC light curve of Sector 110 would give an independent ellipsoidal measurement at roughly the S32 precision (+/- 45 ppm). A second detection near 163 ppm would confirm a ~0.1 solar-mass companion and the candidate should be dropped; a non-detection at that precision would refute the S32 signal as systematics and the candidate should then be proposed for submission with the 17.68 Earth-radius size, A1V host and ellipsoidal caveat noted. Sector 110 would also independently check the transit depth and refine the ephemeris (`fit_period_error_days` 0.00000394).

TRICERATOPS supports an on-target transit but not the mass: `most_likely_scenario` TP on TIC 264626874, `fpp_mean` 0.07462 +/- 0.082 ('likely planet', not validated; the record shows an earlier run at 0.01475). TRICERATOPS does not model a brown-dwarf or late-M companion of this radius on the target, so it does not resolve the ellipsoidal question.

The pipeline-level sector depth disagreement (`depth_ppm_by_sector` S98 2770 +/- 57 vs S32 3385 +/- 45, `sector_depth_consistency_p_value` 2.64e-17) is a QLP-versus-SPOC processing effect rather than a property of the star, because the uniform cutout apertures agree (`cutout_depth_ppm_by_sector_and_aperture` 2694-3096 ppm across both sectors, `cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value` 0.699). This should be noted at submission, not treated as a red flag.

Gaia shows no bright stellar companion: `gaia_ruwe` 1.19, `gaia_non_single_star` 0, `gaia_eclipsing_binary` False, `vsx_binaries` empty. The second LAMOST spectrum (A2V at 4.6 arcsec, RV -20 vs -14 km/s, 'no Gaia source in the fibre') is most simply the same rapidly rotating star in an offset fibre; a 6 km/s shift is not significant at `gaia_vbroad_km_s` 185.

I agree with the mechanical 'held', and with the later agent decision in the record (2026-10-16 04:15) rather than the earlier 'proposed for submission' (2026-10-16 04:12). The earlier decision dismissed 'held' because `released_tess_sectors_not_in_all_sector_verification` is empty, but a sector that TESS is currently observing (`unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star` 110) can decide the single-sector ellipsoidal detection without RV follow-up, and the hold criterion explicitly includes such sectors.
